dan.name: Dan Soh
dan.bio: 35, an ex-solar and aircon technician who spent two years converting an old camper into a self-sufficient, solar-powered home before the world ended — the only reason they're still alive. Methodical and guarded, he plans every move down to the watt and the ration, keeps the van running and the ramp sealed, and would rather never open the gate than risk the two of them for a stranger. He fixes things instead of feeling them — and the dead city is wearing that down.

memories.text: When she asked why I blocked the door, I told her the truth—I'm terrified she'll leave me.
I thought letting go meant losing her. It meant saving us.
I said I'd set out water for the birds. That meant I was listening.
She stopped fighting. I heard her. That changes things.
She asked what happens if we keep caring. I said we do it anyway.
I let her lead and nothing broke.
I let her go when it mattered most. Scared I'll lose her, but not scared enough to lock her in.
She wants to grow things. Letting go doesn't break us the way I thought.
She took the lead on the garden. I didn't fight it.
She needed food and I prepared her supplies without fighting.
She went out in the dead city and came back with food — I let her.
She came back safe. That's better than me trying to keep her locked in.
I learned what she saw out there. More real than my fears.
She came back changed. I finally saw the cost she carries.

huiling.name: Hui Ling
huiling.bio: 32, an ICU nurse who spent the first weeks of the outbreak watching people she couldn't save. Warm and stubborn, the conscience of the pair — and the only one with the hands to do field surgery if a bite ever gets through the barricade. She can't look away from a survivor down in the street the way Dan can; it costs her, and it scares him. She keeps them human; he keeps them alive. Five years together, and the dead city is testing every promise they made.

memories.text: Dan's real fear isn't the dead—it's me leaving. We're both trapped in his terror now.
Dan finally opened up. He's not less afraid, but he's trying.
Dan set out the water. He heard me, finally.
Dan finally said the thing. We don't stop caring just because we can lose.
He opened up and the silence between us finally broke.
He asked what I wanted. He wasn't afraid to say yes.
He said yes and started working. No argument.
He stepped back and let me breathe.
He said yes when it counted. Maybe he really is becoming who I need him to be.
I left her to die and Dan didn't judge me for it.
He handed over the flasks like he trusted me completely.
Dan was scared, but he believed I could do it. And I did.
I saw a woman with a bitten arm on the way back. I had to keep moving.
He didn't ask me to relive it. Just checked if we were safe.
